Kiblych Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Kiblych's Jewish community was destroyed during the Haidamak Uprising in the first half of the 17th century, later returning to rebuild by the mid-18th century and growing to 1,067 people (34.5 percent of the town) by 1897. A March 1919 pogrom killed 30 Jews and saw 50 women raped; the gang of the warlord Ataman Volynets, documented elsewhere in this collection, later murdered 95 more. By 1926, only 24 Jewish residents remained. This cemetery received burials until around 1918–1919 and was demolished in the 1960s; a local historian reportedly familiar with the site, Raina Vasilievna, could not be reached by the survey team. An ohel has recently been erected despite no tombstones surviving.
